source_tensions.subject: Resource-token scope presence
source_tensions.disposition: Treat scope as optional or replaceable. If scope and a companion authorization claim coexist, enforce them independently.
source_tensions.grounding: Core lists scope without marking it REQUIRED and permits a companion authorization claim to replace it; R3 expressly treats scope as optional.

source_tensions.subject: Agent action after event-token expiry
source_tensions.disposition: Apply the stricter MUST NOT behavior.
source_tensions.grounding: The Events draft gives conflicting normative strengths for the same action.

source_tensions.subject: Polymorphic EdDSA in Events examples
source_tensions.disposition: Follow the normative prohibition; do not use the conflicting example as an acceptance vector.
source_tensions.grounding: The normative algorithm rule conflicts with the subscribe-token example.

source_tensions.subject: Signature-Key cached scheme
source_tensions.disposition: Keep the documented behavior opt-in and visibly provisional until the editor source settles it.
source_tensions.grounding: Signature-Key labels the cache design a straw man and open design.

source_tensions.subject: R3 historical bytes after same-URI replacement
source_tensions.disposition: A published R3 URI is immutable in this implementation. Changed exact bytes receive a new URI, and referenced bytes remain retrievable for the required token and audit window.
source_tensions.grounding: The draft permits replacement at one URI while also claiming URI plus hash is a permanently refetchable record.

source_tensions.subject: Operation selected by a protected R3 challenge
source_tensions.disposition: The Resource creates an exact-request R3 document whose operation set equals the validated requested set; an equal set may reuse the same document.
source_tensions.grounding: The general mapping only says a document covers the request, leaving operation selection ambiguous.

source_tensions.subject: AS binding to the Agent requested operation set
source_tensions.disposition: The AS evaluates and grants only from the exact-request document; every granted operation must be a subset of that exact set.
source_tensions.grounding: The AS receives URI and digest but no separately authenticated requested set when a broader document is reused.

source_tensions.subject: Per-delivery replay identity for multi-use subscriptions
source_tensions.disposition: Treat eid only as subscription context. Deduplicate an exact accepted delivery by the SHA-256 of the compact event token, a zero separator, and the exact payload bytes.
source_tensions.grounding: The draft reuses eid for every delivery but tells the Agent to deduplicate by (iss,eid), which would discard every legitimate later event.

source_tensions.subject: Mission proposal policy denial error
source_tensions.disposition: Return provisional 403 mission_denied until Core assigns a registered mission proposal denial.
source_tensions.grounding: A valid mission proposal may be denied by policy, but the mission endpoint error table has no policy-denial result.

source_tensions.subject: Unknown mission reference at the Person Token Endpoint
source_tensions.disposition: Return one identical 400 invalid_request response for absent and wrong-owner mission references at the Person Token Endpoint.
source_tensions.grounding: The endpoint requires rejection but mission_not_found is registered only for a mission own URL.

source_tensions.subject: Resource enforcement of mission expiry without mission content
source_tensions.disposition: Cap a mission-bound Resource token at the verified Person token expiry; the Person Server already capped that token at mission expiry and rechecks retained mission state later.
source_tensions.grounding: Core requires the Resource-token ceiling but deliberately gives the Resource only mission_s256, not the mission expires_at value.

source_tensions.subject: Global uniqueness of a mission digest
source_tensions.disposition: Do not add a private blob member. Reject a colliding retained identifier and seek a source-defined uniqueness rule.
source_tensions.grounding: Two otherwise identical approvals at the same approved_at timestamp have identical bytes and s256 despite the draft's global-uniqueness claim.
blocks: claim that approved_at alone guarantees unique mission identity

source_tensions.subject: Exact bytes identified by an accepted mission update
source_tensions.disposition: Persist and hash the exact authenticated update request body, retaining unknown additive members byte-for-byte.
source_tensions.grounding: Core defines the digest over bytes as the PS persists them but does not say whether the PS may rewrite or canonically re-encode the authenticated request.

source_tensions.subject: Immediate mission action refusal and its error result
source_tensions.disposition: Return provisional 403 mission_update_denied or mission_completion_denied while leaving the active mission unchanged.
source_tensions.grounding: Core defines acceptance, deferred review, and clarification follow-up but neither says whether immediate terminal refusal is allowed nor assigns an error if it is.

source_tensions.subject: Mission action uncertain-success recovery
source_tensions.disposition: Perform one mission-action POST and never retry automatically; do not claim recovery for an uncertain update or person-accepted completion.
source_tensions.grounding: Core provides no request identity or lookup that recovers an update or completion whose acceptance or response delivery became uncertain.

source_tensions.subject: Decision-maker for a mission update
source_tensions.disposition: Follow the update-specific rule and permit the Person Server's update policy to accept autonomously; keep completion person-confirmed.
source_tensions.grounding: The mission overview says the person decides all three operations, while the update section says the PS may accept an update on its own.

source_tensions.subject: Outstanding credentials after mission termination
source_tensions.disposition: Close later Person Server decisions but do not claim that termination revokes already-issued credentials; the Agent must stop using them.
source_tensions.grounding: Core defines no signal by which a Resource that receives only mission_s256 learns that the Person Server terminated the mission.
blocks: claim that mission termination revokes outstanding credentials

source_tensions.subject: Absent Retry-After in a deferred response
source_tensions.disposition: Honor the explicit receiver fallback and use a five-second interval when Retry-After is absent; validate one present value strictly.
source_tensions.grounding: Core marks Retry-After required, then defines a five-second default when the header is absent.
